- `fl.filter_empty(path?: text): <T>[]` — keeps entries that are not empty ("", null, 0, "0", false, [], {}) — the only one of the family that drops them all
- `fl.filter_empty_array(path?: text): <T>[]`
- `fl.filter_empty_object(path?: text): <T>[]`
- `fl.filter_empty_text(path?: text): <T>[]` — drops only `""`; null, 0, false, [] and {} stay
- `fl.filter_false(path?: text): <T>[]`
- `fl.filter_null(path?: text): <T>[]`
- `fl.filter_zero(path?: text): <T>[]` — drops only the integer `0` (strict), not `"0"` or `0.0`
- `fl.find(code: text, timeout?: int): <T>` — `code` is a JS body run per element; returns the first ELEMENT it accepts (`null` when none)
- `fl.findIndex(code: text, timeout?: int): int` — `code` is a JS body run per element; returns the first matching INDEX as an int (`-1` when none)
- `fl.first_notempty(value: any): any` — first value that is not empty ("", null, 0, "0", false, [], {})
- `fl.first_notnull(value: any): any`
- `fl.fsort(path?: text, type?: "text"|"itext"|"natural"|"inatural"|"number", asc?: bool): <T>[]` — `type` is the comparator: "number" (the only numeric one), "text"/"itext" (strcmp/strcasecmp), "natural"/"inatural" ("a2 < a10"). Default "itext"; anything else sorts as text. The path arg drills into each element
- `fl.get(path: text, default?: json): any` — `path` may be a runtime value: after `fl.index_by("suite_id")`, `fl.get(ref("suite.id"))` returns that key's rows (null for a missing key). ⚠ the `default` applies only to a MISSING path — a key present with a `null` value stays `null`; chain `fl.first_notnull(default)` to cover both.
- `fl.gt(value: <T>): bool`
- `fl.gte(value: <T>): bool`
- `fl.has(path: text): bool` — `false` for a missing key and for a key whose value is `null` (unlike `fl.get`'s default, which treats a present null as present)
- `fl.hmac_md5(key: text, raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.hmac_sha1(key: text, raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.hmac_sha256(key: text, raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.hmac_sha384(key: text, raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.hmac_sha512(key: text, raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.icontains(search: text): bool` — case-insensitive; piped value is the subject, the arg is the substring
- `fl.iends_with(search: text): bool` — case-insensitive; piped value is the subject, the arg is the substring
- `fl.in(search: <T>): bool`
- `fl.index_by(path: text): { [key: string]: <T>[] }` — a GROUP-BY: every value is an ARRAY of the items sharing that key, even when only one does, so a lookup reads `idx[key][0]`. Items whose path is missing or non-scalar are dropped
- `fl.istarts_with(search: text): bool` — case-insensitive; piped value is the subject, the arg is the substring
- `fl.join(separator: text): text`
- `fl.jwe_decode(arg1: any)`
- `fl.jwe_encode(arg1: any)`
- `fl.lambda(code: text, timeout?: int): any` — runs a JS body once over the piped value, which it binds as `$this` (NOT `$parent`)
- `fl.log(base: <T>): decimal`
- `fl.lt(value: <T>): bool`
- `fl.lte(value: <T>): bool`
- `fl.ltrim(mask?: text): text`
- `fl.map(code: text, timeout?: int): any[]` — `code` is a JS body run per element, over `$this`/`$index`/`$parent` — build it with `lam.fn`
- `fl.max(bound?: decimal): decimal`
- `fl.md5(raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.min(bound?: decimal): decimal`
- `fl.mod(value: int): int`
- `fl.mul(value: decimal): decimal`
- `fl.ne(value: <T>): bool`
- `fl.num_max(value: any): decimal`
- `fl.num_min(value: any): decimal`
- `fl.number_format(decimals: int, decimal_separator: text, thousands_separator: text): string`
- `fl.pick(keys: text): <T>`
- `fl.pow(exp: <T>): decimal`
- `fl.prepend(value: <T>, path: text): <T>[]`
- `fl.range(start: int, stop: int): int[]`
- `fl.reduce(initial_value: any, code: text, timeout?: int): any` — `code` is a JS body run per element; the ACCUMULATOR is `$result` (there is no `$acc`) and `initial_value` is REQUIRED. `initial_value` takes ANY value (an object/text accumulator, `c.obj({...})`/`c.text("")`, not just an int); the result is that accumulator
- `fl.regex_match(subject: text): text[]` — piped value is the PATTERN, the arg is the subject — see `regex_test`
- `fl.regex_match_all(subject: text): text[]` — piped value is the PATTERN, the arg is the subject — see `regex_test`
- `fl.regex_quote(delimiter?: text): text`
- `fl.regex_replace(replacement: text, subject: text): text` — piped value is the PATTERN, `subject` is the text searched — see `regex_test`. The replacement comes FIRST
- `fl.regex_test(subject: text): bool` — piped value is the PATTERN (build it with `c.regex(...)`); the arg is the subject — the REVERSE of `contains`/`starts_with`. Swapped args → always false, no error. Write `withFilters(c.regex("^a+$"), fl.regex_test(inp("s")))` (or name the arg: `fl.regex_test({ subject: inp("s") })`). A pattern found in the subject slot is refused at build time
- `fl.round(precision?: int): decimal`
- `fl.rtrim(mask?: text): text`
- `fl.secureid_decode(salt: text): int` — a wrong salt, or a garbage/empty id, is a 400 (`This signature is invalid.` / `Invalid input format for secureId.`), NOT null — wrap in s.try_catch to handle a miss; only the id from `secureid_encode` of a non-negative int round-trips back
- `fl.secureid_encode(salt: text): text` — the operand must be a NON-NEGATIVE integer — a negative or fractional one encodes without error but `secureid_decode` returns a DIFFERENT positive int (`-3` → `13`, `-42` → `214`, `1.5` → `1`), NOT a round-trip; validate the domain before encoding
- `fl.set(path: text, value: any): any`
- `fl.set_conditional(path: text, value: any, conditional: any): any`
- `fl.set_ifnotempty(path: text, value: any): any`
- `fl.set_ifnotnull(path: text, value: any): any`
- `fl.sha1(raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.sha256(raw?: bool): text` — the optional `raw` arg returns RAW binary, not the hex digest — fl.bin2hex()/fl.base64_encode() it before returning or storing (strlen then UNDER-COUNTS: it counts characters, not bytes); omit `raw` for hex
- `fl.sha384(raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.sha512(raw?: bool): text`
- `fl.some(code: text, timeout?: int): bool` — `code` is a JS body run per element (true for any?), over `$this`/`$index`/`$parent` — returns a BOOL (`false` on an empty list)
- `fl.splice(offset: int, length?: int, path?: text): <T>[]` — returns the REMOVED slice, not the remainder — [1,2,3,4] spliced at offset 1 length 2 yields [2,3]; with a `path` it removes in place and returns the whole value instead
- `fl.split(separator: text): text[]`
- `fl.starts_with(search: text): bool` — piped value is the subject text; the arg is the substring searched for
- `fl.string_replace(search: text, replacement: text): text`
- `fl.strip_tags(exclude?: text): text`
- `fl.stripos(search: text): int|false`
- `fl.strpos(search: text): int|false`
- `fl.sub(value: decimal): decimal`
- `fl.substr(start: int, length: int): text`
- `fl.to_epoch_day(timezone?: text): int`
- `fl.to_epoch_hour(timezone?: text): int`
- `fl.to_epoch_minute(timezone?: text): int`
- `fl.to_epoch_ms(timezone?: text): int`
- `fl.to_epoch_sec(timezone?: text): int`
- `fl.to_epochms(timezone?: text): epochms`
- `fl.transform(expression: text): any` — `expression` is Xano Expression Engine source, NOT a JS body — no `return`, and the piped value is `$0` (or `$$`), NOT `$this` (which is null here). `$var`/`$input`/`$env`/`$auth` resolve and filters pipe inside it: `$0 * 2`, `$0|sort|join:","`. Parenthesize a pipe inside an object literal — `{ s: ($0|sort|join:",") }` — or its comma is read as the key separator and later keys vanish silently. For JavaScript use `lambda`
- `fl.trim(mask?: text): text`
- `fl.unique(path?: text): <T>[]` — with a `path`, dedupes a list of records by the value at that path and keeps the FIRST per key — but it DROPS every element whose path is missing or null (the same rule as `index_by`), so deduping by an optional key loses those rows
- `fl.unpick(keys: text): <T>` — returns the object without the named keys (inverse of a pick)
- `fl.unset(path: text): any`
- `fl.url_addarg(key: text, value: text, encoding_rfc3986?: bool): text`
- `fl.url_delarg(key: text): text`
- `fl.url_getarg(key: text, default?: text): text`
- `fl.url_hasarg(key: text): bool`
- `fl.yaml_encode(options?: bool, inline?: int, indent?: int): text`

Zero-argument filters, by operand type: array: array_entries, array_keys, array_lower, array_pop, array_shift, array_shuffle, array_values, count, first, flatten, last, reverse, rsort, safe_array; comparison: empty, even, is_array, is_bool, is_decimal, is_int, is_object, is_text, is_uuid, not, null, odd; geo: to_geo_linestring, to_geo_multilinestring, to_geo_multipoint, to_geo_multipolygon, to_geo_point, to_geo_polygon; math: abs, acos, acosh, asin, asinh, atan, atanh, avg, bitwise_not, ceil, cos, deg2rad, exp, floor, ln, log10, product, rad2deg, sin, sqrt, sum, tan; other: sort; security: uid, uuid4; text: addslashes, capitalize, escape, from_utf8, list_encodings, lower, querystring_parse, sql_alias, sql_esc, strip_accents, strlen, text_escape, text_unescape, to_utf8, upper, url_parse; timestamp: ms_to_secs, secs_to_ms; transform: base64_decode, base64_decode_urlsafe, base64_encode, base64_encode_urlsafe, bin2hex, bindec, create_object_from_entries, decbin, dechex, decoct, hex2bin, hexdec, json_decode, json_encode, octdec, to_bool, to_decimal, to_expr, to_int, to_text, url_decode, url_decode_rfc3986, url_encode, url_encode_rfc3986, xml_decode, yaml_decode.
`fl.reverse()` reverses a list only: on a text value it answers the text UNCHANGED, with no error.
An unknown `timezone` (a typo, `+05:30`, `PDT`) silently means UTC. A literal warns at export; take a runtime zone as an `input.enum`.
`fl.to_bool()` is NOT a truthiness cast: it accepts only the boolean vocabulary — `true`/`1`/`"1"`/`"true"`/`"on"`/`"yes"` and `false`/`0`/`"0"`/`"false"`/`"off"`/`""` — and ANY other value 400s `ERROR_CODE_INPUT_ERROR` "Invalid boolean input.". For a truthiness cast pipe `fl.ne(c.int(0))`.

Variadic filters — they take arguments, but no declared list, so the count is not checked: sprintf.

# Lambda bodies (JavaScript)

> Read when writing a JavaScript body, or weighing whether to reach for one at all — `lam.fn`, `fl.lambda`, `fl.reduce`, `s.lambda`; each surface binds a different set of identifiers.

**A lambda is an escape hatch, not a default.** Use one only when a native filter,
an `expr(...)`/`obj(...)` expression, or a statement can't do the work: each call crosses a
process boundary into a BOUNDED pool of lambda workers every lambda in the workspace shares.
The crossing is per CALL, not per element — an iterating filter sends the body ONCE and loops on the
other side, so one iterating filter over a list beats a lambda inside a stack loop.

The lambda statement (`s.lambda({ as, code, timeout? })`) and eight filters run a
JavaScript body. **Write the body as a FUNCTION, not a `c.text` string** (bindings are
typed parameters; a wrong name is a compile error). Inline, the surface is implied by where it sits:

```ts
fl.map(({ $this }) => $this * 2)                                   // map's bindings, typed from the position
fl.reduce({ initial_value: 0, code: ({ $result, $this }) => $result + $this })
s.lambda({ as: "total", code: ({ $var }) => $var.subtotal * 1.2 })  // ambient only — $this is a compile error
```

Destructure bindings by their exact names (`({ $this })`). Refused: `(b) => b.$this`,
renaming (`{ $this: x }`), nesting, defaults, rest.

⚠ An inline `code:` arrow receives BINDINGS ONLY. `capture` is an option of
`lam.fn`, not a field of `s.lambda` or a filter, so `capture:` beside `code:` is a type
error — move the body into `lam.fn(fn, { capture })` (below).

For a body built away from its call site:

- `lam.fn(({ $result, $this }) => $result + $this, { surface?, capture? })` — name a `surface` to check it here, or omit it and the call site checks it.
- `lam.raw("return 1", { surface })` — text, same validation.
- `lam.raw(code, { surface, unchecked: true })` — sends a body that does not parse or declares a top-level `import`/`export`; skips those syntax checks only, here and at the `s.lambda` / `fl.*` site.
- `lam.file("./lambdas/total.ts")` — a default-exported function in its own module (path relative to the caller), read as text at build time. NODE ONLY: `import { lam } from "@xano/sdk/node"` (isomorphic `lam` has no `file`). Only the default export's BODY is sent, so a value import, a second export or a top-level helper is refused — move helpers inside; `import type` / `import { type X }` are free. `@xano/sdk/lambda-globals` types the globals below program-wide: keep modules in `xano/lambdas/` (its scaffold tsconfig loads it) or `import type {} from` it under their own tsconfig.

Nothing from the enclosing scope crosses: the body is sent as TEXT, so a closed-over
`const rate` is undefined there (a wrong VALUE at HTTP 200, not an error). Put what the
body needs in `capture`; it arrives as the SECOND parameter, emitted as a `const` prelude:

```ts
lam.fn(({ $this }, { capturedRate }) => $this * capturedRate, { surface: "map", capture: { capturedRate: rate } })
```

⚠ A capture key must NOT share a module-scope binding's name (a `.ts` loader renames one;
refused at build time) — `capture: { capturedRate: rate }`, not `{ rate }`.

Capture JSON data only: a function, `NaN`, a sparse/typed array or class instance (`Date`, `Map`…)
is refused at build time, at any depth. Capture the plain form and rebuild in
the body (`d.getTime()` → `new Date(d)`).

A body is a FUNCTION BODY: it must `return` its value. Bindings by surface — an
identifier outside its surface's set is undefined at runtime, and the SDK refuses
it at build time whichever spelling you use:

- every surface: `$env` · `$input` · `$var` · `$auth` (+ the `console` / `crypto` globals)
- `fl.lambda`: + `$this`
- `fl.map` · `fl.filter` · `fl.some` · `fl.every` · `fl.find` · `fl.findIndex`: + `$this` · `$index` · `$parent`
- `fl.reduce`: + `$this` · `$index` · `$parent` · `$result`
- `s.lambda`: ambient only — no `$this`, no `$parent`, no `$result`.

`$result` is `reduce`'s ACCUMULATOR (there is no `$acc`). `$this` is the element in
an iterating filter and the piped value in `fl.lambda`; `$parent` is the whole array
and exists only on the iterating filters. A stack variable is reached as
`$var.name` — it is NOT also injected as a bare `$name`.

`$auth` with no authenticated caller (a public surface, or an authed one reached without a
token) is `{ id: 0, dbo: "" }`, not null. Test `$auth.id > 0`, not truthiness.

Hazards:

- ⚠ A body that THROWS or times out does not fail the request (nor reach `s.try_catch`): the
  engine returns its diagnostic TEXT as the value with HTTP 200 (`"[Line 1:Char 7] boom"`,
  `"Lambda timed out after 1 seconds"`; a thrown non-Error is `" Unknown error"` on the cloud).
  Validate before consuming it. To FAIL the request: wrap the body in `try { return { ok: true,
  v } } catch { return { ok: false } }`, then `s.precondition` `ref("r.ok", { safe: true })` = `true`.
- ⚠ An `s.lambda` whose body returns a STRING that parses as a JSON object or array binds
  the DECODED value, not the string (the statement's output is cast as `json`);
  scalar-looking strings (`"123"`, `"true"`) stay text, and `fl.map`/`fl.lambda` keep
  the string. A body that `JSON.stringify`s a payload to sign/hash/store gets an object
  back. To keep text, return it WRAPPED (`{ text }`) and read `.text`.
- ⚠ `timeout` is COOPERATIVE — observed only at an `await` — so it bounds WAITING (a slow
  `fetch`), not compute: a 1s `timeout` over a 3s busy-loop runs all 3s and returns
  normally. Bound a loop that could run away inside the body.
- ⚠ A top-level `import`/`export` is a syntax error — the body is a function body. Reach
  a dependency through the PRELOADED globals below. A dynamic `import("…")`/`require("…")`
  with a LITERAL specifier is not portable: an instance that bundles the body first
  returns the TEXT `Could not resolve "node:crypto"` with HTTP 200.
- Preloaded globals — no specifier, so these work everywhere:
  `_` · `aws4` · `axios` · `cryptojs` · `DateTime` · `ethers` · `fastXmlParser` ·
  `jose` · `luxon` · `mailparser` · `math` · `moment` · `nodemailer` · `socks` ·
  `uuid` · `utils`
  …plus `fetch`, `Buffer`, `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, and the `crypto` above
  (`randomUUID`, `createHmac`, `createHash`, `subtle`). `Object.keys(globalThis)`
  inside a body lists whatever else a given instance carries.
- An INLINE body in `xano/` that uses one of these globals does not type-check until that
  file has `import type {} from "@xano/sdk/lambda-globals"` at the top (safe in the defs
  program — it is not the frontend); or move the body to a `lam.file` module under
  `xano/lambdas/`, whose scaffold tsconfig loads the types already.
- ⚠ `console` output goes to the request LOG, not stdout. The logging methods (`log` ·
  `error` · `warn` · `info` · `debug` · `trace`), plus `table` and `dir`, all route there;
  `group`/`count`/`time`/`assert` are undefined, and CALLING one throws (error text as the
  value, HTTP 200).

TypeScript annotations survive in the body, and top-level `await` works.

Inline and `lam.fn` bodies are stored WHITESPACE-MINIFIED on one line, so an error position
(`[Line 1:Char 59]`) always says Line 1. Use `lam.file` when you want the body readable or
line-accurate errors; its module text is stored as written.

# Lock file

> Read when a `xano.lock` exists or should — renaming/pruning/importing identities, seeding the lock programmatically, or asking which commands write it.

`xano.lock` pins each object's guid and each api-group/toolset canonical, so renames
stay renames (guids otherwise derive from `(type, name)`; a query's from `(api group,
verb, name)`). Committed. A composed entry is keyed by that identity —
`query:<group>|<verb>|<name>`, `channel:<server>|<path>`, `message:<server>|<path>|<name>`
— its guid's seed; a bare `query:<name>` key is rewritten to the composed form by the next locked export.

- `npx @xano/sdk lock rename <kind> <old> <new>` — `kind` is the SDK kind (`table`, `apiGroup`) or stored key (`dbo`).
  Run it when `export` names it after a rename in code (it prints the command); the next export emits the original guid under the new name.
  Reads the `index.ts` beside the lock (or `--entry`); refused while `<old>` is still exported. Composed names go in full; renaming a parent moves them.
- `npx @xano/sdk lock prune <entry-file> [keys…] --yes` — drops orphaned entries. Finding orphans
  RUNS the entry's module scope (env assertions included); `--identity-only --yes <key>…`
  prunes named keys (`table:users`) with no evaluation and no orphan check.
- `npx @xano/sdk lock import <live-bundle.json> [--yes]` — seed the lock from a `workspace export`
  to take over an existing workspace (a compiled bundle is refused).
- Every lock subcommand accepts `--lock=<path>`; from outside the lock's directory pass it.
- Merge conflict: keep both sides; two keys on one guid → `lock rename` onto the kept
  name, or `lock prune --identity-only --yes` the other.
- Programmatic use: call `seedLockOverrides(readLockFile(path))` BEFORE importing any def
  module — references bake guids at import time; `writeBundle` refuses an unseeded lock.

### Writers and readers

- `export`/`deploy`/`release`/`preflight` of an ENTRY FILE update the lock; `compile`/`routes` only READ.
- `--no-lock` builds without one (names derive guids, the instance invents public URLs, no `--prune`);
  REFUSED over a parseable lock.
- A DEPLOY or a RELEASE writes back only `landed`: what this project LANDED on each destination
  (ephemerals: `.xano/ephemeral.json`). `--prune` deletes only that, never a merely exported name;
  no record there, no prune until one landing. Commit the lock.
- A `deploy` (`--replace` too) PRESERVES the archive's guids, so the lock still describes the rebuilt workspace.

### CI

- `--frozen-lock` fails (`SDK_DRIFT`) instead of changing the lock, and fails while the lock carries
  an entry no exported object matches. A plain `export` only warns and writes that entry down, after
  which a rename and a deletion look the same. Resolve it with `lock rename` or `lock prune`, or
  accept them with `--allow-lock-orphans` when they are the not-yet-ported half of an adopted workspace.
- `export --check` implies `--frozen-lock` and writes nothing — no bundle, no lock — so it
  reads no `xano/.env` or `.secrets.json` and refuses the flags that supply them. `npm run xano:check` runs it,
  so CI needs no secrets.
- With no lock at all, either flag fails only when the source has identities to record (an empty workspace passes).

# Legacy paradigms and retired statements

> Read when the code was PULLED from an existing Xano instance — how a codegen'd tree reads, the shapes in it that must not be "fixed", and any `raw({ name: "mvp:…" })`, `realtimeTrigger()`, or name the catalogs do not list.

Shapes codegen emits when it decodes an existing workspace, all supported.
**Do not author these.** They are listed by name only so you recognize them
in pulled code rather than "fixing" them; each line names what to use instead.

"realtime" and "channel" name objects in both lists: a matching name does NOT mean
the same object; check which list it came from.

- `c.expressionLegacy` — the older `const:expr` expression form, emitted by codegen for workspaces that still hold one — author `c.expression` instead.
- `realtimeTrigger()` — the SUPERSEDED realtime trigger, against the workspace-global realtime layer — a different object from the current `channel`, despite the similar name. For a join hook use `realtimeChannelTrigger({ actions: { join: true } })`; for message handling use a `realtimeMessage()` handler, which is the equivalent of its `message` action (a message is its own object, not a trigger action).
- `s.api.realtime_event` — publishes to the SUPERSEDED workspace-global realtime layer, NOT to a `realtimeChannel()` — its `channel` is a string against that layer, so pointing it at a current-layer channel path publishes into the void. Use `s.realtime.publish` instead: it names the owning `realtimeServer()`, so it addresses a real `realtimeChannel()`.

Retired statements and statement VERSIONS — no `s.` surface exists. Pulled code shows
them as `raw({ name: "…" })` and they keep running as stored, so leave them; author
the replacement only for NEW code. Never swap one for the other — the stored shapes differ.

- `mvp:crypto_jwe_decode` → `mvp:crypto_jwe_decode2`
- `mvp:crypto_jwe_encode` → `mvp:crypto_jwe_encode3`
- `mvp:crypto_jwe_encode2` → `mvp:crypto_jwe_encode3`
- `mvp:crypto_jws_decode` → `mvp:crypto_jws_decode2`
- `mvp:crypto_jws_encode` → `mvp:crypto_jws_encode2`
- `mvp:connect_ncscale_send_log` — retired, no replacement
- `mvp:dbo_get` → `mvp:dbo_getby`
- `mvp:guid` — retired, no replacement

Statements the engine writes but will NOT import back — no `s.` surface exists, and
unlike the retired versions above these must be FIXED, not left alone. Pulled code shows
them as `raw({ name: "…" })`; `export()` refuses any bundle that still contains one.

- `mvp:placeholder` — an unconfigured statement slot the engine writes for a statement it could not resolve. Importing a workspace that contains one fails with "Missing statement: mvp:placeholder" on every destination; replace it with the statement it stands in for before deploying.

## Reading a pulled tree

`codegen` emits objects as FACTORY calls (`table({...})`, `query({...})`, …) — the form
you author by hand — so inference survives the round trip.
Three shapes read differently and must not be "fixed": a trigger its factory cannot
reproduce (its target outside the pulled tree, or `meta` it cannot write) stays
`{...} satisfies TriggerDef`; a
statement the catalog cannot model round-trips verbatim through `raw()`
(`@xano/sdk/codegen`); and an object ALREADY EMPTY upstream decodes to a def with
no `stack`, reported as `empty-source` — faithful, not a decode failure. Workspace env
var VALUES go to `xano/.env` (owner-only, gitignored); `xano/workspace.ts` declares each as `""`.

Markers for stored shapes the checks refuse — keep them, not for new code:
`uncheckedAs: true`, `lam.raw(body, { unchecked: true })`, `rawWhere([...])` from
`@xano/sdk/codegen` (view filter), `"key" as never` (a key the target dropped; remove once declared).

# Statement catalog

> Read for the field signature of a specific statement — every surface, grouped by `s.*` namespace.

`[special]`: hand-written signature (`llms.txt` Specials, `llms/statements-*`). `[output]`: the engine's output flag; in-place mutators carrying it (`s.math.add`, `bitwise.*`) still take no `as`.

### (top-level)

`s.throw` raises a named error `s.try_catch` catches; uncaught, it answers HTTP 200 `{ payload, statement: "Throw Error" }`, or its `status` (100–599) when it sets one. Inside `s.db.transaction` a throw or failed precondition rolls it back.

- `s.foreach` [special]
- `s.group` [special]
- `s.lambda({ as?: string; code: value; timeout?: value })`
- `s.precondition({ expr: comparison; error_type?: "standard" | "notfound" | "toomanyrequests" | "accessdenied" | "unauthorized" | "badrequest" | "inputerror"; error?: value; payload?: value })`
- `s.return` [special]
- `s.switch` [special]
- `s.throw({ name?: string; value: value; status?: number })`
- `s.try_catch` [special]
- `s.update_var` [special]

### array

`by` is a `$this` expression, NOT a column name: `by: ref("$this.id")` (warns `stack.array-key-constant`). A predicate's `if` binds `$this` only; `$index` only in `partition` (warns `stack.array-index-unbound`).

- `s.array.difference({ as?: string; expr: value; value: value; by?: value })`
- `s.array.every({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })` [output] → as: boolean
- `s.array.filter_count({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })`
- `s.array.filter({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })`
- `s.array.find_index({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })`
- `s.array.find({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })` [output]
- `s.array.group_by({ as?: string; expr: value; by?: value })`
- `s.array.has({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })`
- `s.array.intersection({ as?: string; expr: value; value: value; by?: value })`
- `s.array.map` [special]
- `s.array.merge({ name: string; value: value })` [output]
- `s.array.partition({ expr: value; as?: string; if: comparison })`
- `s.array.pop({ name: string; as?: string })` [output]
- `s.array.push({ name: string; value: value })` [output]
- `s.array.shift({ name: string; as?: string })`
- `s.array.union` [special]
- `s.array.unshift({ name: string; value: value })`

### debug

`s.debug.stop` is a REAL terminator: it ends the request with HTTP 200 `{ payload, statement: "Stop & Debug" }` (use `s.precondition` for an error status). Also exported flat as `die()`; there is no `s.die`.

- `s.debug.log({ value: value })`
- `s.debug.stop({ value: value })`

### expect

Assertions. Use only in a `workflowTest({...})` stack, asserting on what a `.call` bound with `as`; elsewhere a failure aborts the request with HTTP 500 and the assertion's message (`to_equal failed - expected value 2 does not equal 1`). `to_throw` sees only an error carrying a MESSAGE, so an empty-message failure (`ERROR_CODE_ACCESS_DENIED`) reports "response is ok", and `to_be_within` EXCLUDES both bounds — `min < expr < max`.

- `s.expect.to_be_defined({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_empty({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_false({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_greater_than({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_in_the_future({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_in_the_past({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_less_than({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_null({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_true({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_be_within({ expr: value; min: value; max: value })`
- `s.expect.to_contain({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_end_with({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_equal({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_match({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_not_be_defined({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_not_be_null({ expr: value })`
- `s.expect.to_not_equal({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_start_with({ expr: value; value: value })`
- `s.expect.to_throw` [special]

### security

- `s.security.check_password({ as?: string; text_password: value; hash_password: value })` [output] → as: boolean (true when the plaintext matches the stored hash. ⚠ not input.password — pass input.text() plaintext. ⚠ THROWS 500 on a non-hash hash_password (Invalid password syntax.))
- `s.security.create_auth_token` [special]
- `s.security.create_curve_key({ as?: string; curve?: "P-256" | "P-384" | "P-521"; format?: "object" | "base64" })`
- `s.security.create_password({ as?: string; character_count?: value; require_lowercase?: value; require_uppercase?: value; require_digit?: value; require_symbol?: value; symbol_whitelist?: value })`

- `s.security.create_secret_key({ as?: string; bits?: value; format?: "object" | "base64" })`
- `s.security.create_uuid({ as?: string })`
- `s.security.decrypt({ as?: string; data: value; algorithm?: "aes-128-cbc" | "aes-192-cbc" | "aes-256-cbc" | "aes-128-gcm" | "aes-192-gcm" | "aes-256-gcm"; key: value; iv: value })` → as: unknown (the plaintext; takes encrypt's RAW bytes (fl.base64_decode() a stored base64 first). ⚠ THROWS 500 on a wrong key/iv or non-ciphertext — wrap in s.try_catch)
- `s.security.encrypt({ as?: string; data: value; algorithm?: "aes-128-cbc" | "aes-192-cbc" | "aes-256-cbc" | "aes-128-gcm" | "aes-192-gcm" | "aes-256-gcm"; key: value; iv: value })`
- `s.security.jwe_decode({ as?: string; token: value; key: value; check_claims?: value; key_algorithm?: "A128KW" | "A192KW" | "A256KW" | "A128GCMKW" | "A192GCMKW" | "A256GCMKW" | "ECDH-ES+A128KW" | "ECDH-ES+A192KW" | "ECDH-ES+A256KW"; content_algorithm?: "A128GCM" | "A192GCM" | "A256GCM" | "A128CBC-HS256" | "A192CBC-HS384" | "A256CBC-HS512"; timeDrift?: value })` → as: unknown (the decoded claims. ⚠ THROWS 500 ERROR_FATAL on ANY failure (bad/expired token, wrong key/algorithm, failed check_claims) — wrap in s.try_catch for a 401 (statements-calls.md))
- `s.security.jwe_encode({ as?: string; headers?: value; claims?: value; key: value; key_algorithm?: "A128KW" | "A192KW" | "A256KW" | "A128GCMKW" | "A192GCMKW" | "A256GCMKW" | "ECDH-ES+A128KW" | "ECDH-ES+A192KW" | "ECDH-ES+A256KW"; content_algorithm?: "A128GCM" | "A192GCM" | "A256GCM" | "A128CBC-HS256" | "A192CBC-HS384" | "A256CBC-HS512"; ttl?: value })`
- `s.security.jws_decode({ as?: string; token: value; key: value; check_claims?: value; signature_algorithm?: "PS256" | "PS384" | "PS512" | "RS256" | "RS384" | "RS512" | "HS256" | "HS384" | "HS512" | "ES256" | "ES384" | "ES512"; timeDrift?: value })` → as: unknown (the decoded claims. ⚠ THROWS 500 ERROR_FATAL on ANY failure (bad/garbage/expired/tampered token, wrong key/signature_algorithm, failed check_claims) — wrap in s.try_catch for a 401 (statements-calls.md))
- `s.security.jws_encode({ as?: string; headers?: value; claims?: value; key: value; signature_algorithm?: "PS256" | "PS384" | "PS512" | "RS256" | "RS384" | "RS512" | "HS256" | "HS384" | "HS512" | "ES256" | "ES384" | "ES512"; ttl?: value })`
- `s.security.random_bytes({ as?: string; length?: value })` → as: string (RAW bytes (encrypt too) — fl.bin2hex()/fl.base64_encode() before returning or storing; raw binary mangles in a JSON/text response)
- `s.security.random_number({ as?: string; min?: value; max?: value })`

### storage

- `s.storage.create_attachment({ as?: string; value: value; access?: "public" | "private" = "public"; filename?: value; include_meta?: boolean; type?: value })` → as: XanoFileRef (the stored file VALUE ({ access, path, name, type, size, mime, meta }) — write it into an f.attachment() cell. ⚠ include_meta: true binds the file's internal RECORD instead (id, guid, sig, the storage BUCKET name): never store it as the file value or return it (warns storage.include-meta-returned). type (also optional) coerces the kind when it is image/video/audio)
- `s.storage.create_audio({ as?: string; value: value; access?: "public" | "private" = "public"; filename?: value })` [output]
- `s.storage.create_file_resource({ as?: string; filename: value; filedata: value })` [output]
- `s.storage.create_image({ as?: string; value: value; access?: "public" | "private" = "public"; filename?: value })` [output]
- `s.storage.create_video({ as?: string; value: value; access?: "public" | "private" = "public"; filename?: value })` [output]
- `s.storage.delete_file({ pathname: value })` [output]
- `s.storage.read_file_resource({ as?: string; value: value })` → as: { name; size; mime; data: <contents> }
- `s.storage.sign_private_url({ as?: string; pathname: value; ttl?: value })`

### task

### text

`name` is an EXISTING variable the statement acts on. `trim`/`ltrim`/`rtrim`/`append`/`prepend` rewrite it IN PLACE and take no `as` (a non-text var is coerced, a null reads as `""`); on the trims `value` is a SET OF CHARACTERS to strip, not a substring (`"abcHIcba"` trimmed by `"abc"` → `"HI"`). The predicates (`contains`/`icontains`/`starts_with`/`istarts_with`/`ends_with`/`iends_with`) leave `name` unchanged and bind a boolean to `as` — without `as` they compute nothing (warns `stack.predicate-unbound`); an empty or omitted needle is `true`. An undeclared `name` 500s `Missing var entry`.

- `s.text.append({ name: string; value: value })`
- `s.text.contains({ name: string; as?: string; value: value })` → as: boolean
- `s.text.ends_with({ name: string; as?: string; value: value })` → as: boolean
- `s.text.icontains({ name: string; as?: string; value: value })` → as: boolean
- `s.text.iends_with({ name: string; as?: string; value: value })` → as: boolean
- `s.text.istarts_with({ name: string; as?: string; value: value })` → as: boolean
- `s.text.ltrim({ name: string; value: value })`
- `s.text.prepend({ name: string; value: value })`
- `s.text.rtrim({ name: string; value: value })`
- `s.text.starts_with({ name: string; as?: string; value: value })` → as: boolean
- `s.text.trim({ name: string; value: value })`

### trigger

### util

`s.util.sleep`'s `value` is in SECONDS; a decimal is allowed (`c.decimal(0.5)` = 500 ms); a negative value returns at once. `s.util.set_header`'s `value` is a WHOLE `"Name: value"` line (there is no `name` field) — `c.text("X-Thing: on")`; a line with no colon sends an empty header, and a `Content-Type` line is IGNORED when the response is an object/JSON (it applies to a `c.text()` response). `s.util.template_engine`'s `value` is a Twig template with `$var`/`$input` in scope (`"Hello {{ $var.who }}"`); output is NOT HTML-escaped, a missing var renders `""`, and a syntax error 500s.

- `s.util.geo_distance({ as?: string; latitude_1: value; longitude_1: value; latitude_2: value; longitude_2: value })` → as: number (great-circle distance in METRES (a decimal) — divide by 1000 for km. Identical points return 0)
- `s.util.get_all_input({ as?: string })` → as: unknown (inside an ATTACHED middleware it is a { type, vars } envelope whose vars DIFFERS BY PHASE: pre → the request inputs; post → { status, result }, NOT the request — read the request in post with s.util.get_raw_input. ⚠ status is the STRING "ok" | "exception" (NOT an HTTP code), so store it in a text column, not f.int(); on "exception", result is the { code, message, payload } error and payload is set. See llms/kinds-core.md)
- `s.util.get_env({ as?: string })` → as: Record<string, string> (every workspace env var (declared AND dashboard) as one { NAME: value } object, each value TEXT — so this binds every SECRET; never return it to a client or write it to a row)
- `s.util.get_input` [special]
- `s.util.get_raw_input` [special]
- `s.util.get_vars({ as?: string })`
- `s.util.ip_lookup({ as?: string; value: value })` → as: IpLookupResult | null (NESTED, not flat: { continent: {code,name}, country: {code,name}, region: {code,name}, city: {name}, postal: {code}, location: {latitude, longitude, tz, radius} } — ref("geo.location.latitude"), ref("geo.city.name"); radius is KILOMETRES. ⚠ Every leaf is nullable (region/city/postal often null on a normal hit). `city` is an OBJECT: a bare ref("geo.city") into a text column fails and { safe: true } does NOT help; drill to city.name. The whole var is null for an unresolvable address)
- `s.util.post_process` [special]
- `s.util.send_email({ as?: string; api_key?: value; service_provider?: "resend" | "xano"; subject?: value; message?: value; to?: value; bcc?: value; cc?: value; from?: value; reply_to?: value; scheduled_at?: value })`
- `s.util.set_header({ value: value; duplicates?: "replace" | "append" })`
- `s.util.sleep({ value: value })`
- `s.util.template_engine({ as?: string; value: value })`
